evidence: services/src/main/java/org/keycloak/protocol/oidc/encode/AccessTokenContext.java:72-73 — line 72 checks grantType, then line 73 checks grantType again but with the message 'Null rawTokenId not allowed'. rawTokenId is never null-checked, so a null rawTokenId gets stored (line 77). DefaultTokenContextEncoderProvider.encodeTokenId (line 114-117) would then produce e.g. 'onrtac:null'. Fix: Objects.requireNonNull(rawTokenId, ...).

testsuite/integration-arquillian/tests/base/src/test/java/org/keycloak/testsuite/AssertEvents.java:476-485 — `if (items[0].substring(3, 5).equals(expectedGrantShortcut)) return false;` really is inverted: it rejects when the grant matches. But the claimed effect, 'all test assertions using this matcher fail', is wrong. Because of the wrong indices (issue 2), substring(3,5) of 'onrtac' is 'ta' and never equals 'ac', 'rt', 'dg' or 'ci', so the check never fires and the matcher always passes when the UUID part is valid. The two bugs cancel out, so the grant type is silently never verified in expectCodeToToken/expectDeviceCodeToToken/expectRefresh/expectAuthReqIdToToken (lines 145, 173, 182, 244). It needs fixing (use `!equals`) together with the indices.

AssertEvents.java:483 uses items[0].substring(3, 5). The encoding is sessionType(2)+tokenType(2)+grant(2), per DefaultTokenContextEncoderProvider.java:114-117 and the decoder's encodedContext.substring(4, 6) at DefaultTokenContextEncoderProvider.java:81. So the grant shortcut is at indices 4-5 and substring(4, 6) is correct. Right now the code extracts the last char of the token type plus the first char of the grant (e.g. 'ta').

AssertEvents.java:482 comment says 'Grant type shortcut starts at character 4th char'. Counting from 1, the grant starts at the 5th char (0-based index 4), as the decoder comment at DefaultTokenContextEncoderProvider.java:78 shows ('First 2 chars are sessionType, next 2 chars tokenType, last 2 chars grantType'). The comment matches the buggy substring(3,5), so it should be corrected together with issue 2 (e.g. 'starts at index 4'). This is a minor documentation fix.

server-spi-private/src/main/java/org/keycloak/protocol/oidc/grants/OAuth2GrantTypeFactory.java:30 Javadoc says 'usually like 3-letters shortcut'. Every implementation returns 2 chars: ac, rt, cc, ro, pc, te, pg, ci, dg (e.g. AuthorizationCodeGrantTypeFactory.java:32, ClientCredentialsGrantTypeFactory.java:40). The default decoder requires exactly 2 chars: it rejects contexts whose length is not 6 (DefaultTokenContextEncoderProvider.java:74) and uses substring(4,6). So a 3-letter shortcut would actually break decoding. The Javadoc is a leftover from the first-commit format and should say the shortcut must be 2 characters.
